messages:
Maya R: incident-bot flagged sustained 5xxs from Cygnus (enterprise-vpc) in us-west1 ~ 00:00 UTC. seeing ~30% errors on /v1/generate from dedicated pool cygnus-dpool-us-west1. paging SRE Rotation and oncall.
oncall-bot: Paging SRE Rotation: High error rate, service=redwood-inference, region=us-west1, tenant=cygnus, severity=sev2. Links: https://ops.redwood/incident/1888888000
Jordan K: I'm on it. quick check: are hosts in cygnus-dpool-us-west1 reporting OOMs or kernel panics?
Priya S: ssh'ed to a few nodes, gpu mem looks fine. CPU on the pool head is pegged ~98% and k8s kube-proxy flapping on two nodes. suspect control-plane networking impacting routing -> requests hitting fallback path causing overload.
Lars E: Confirmed k8s events spammed with "node not ready" for gpunode-12 and gpunode-13. kubelet logs show repeated CNI timeouts. could be a regional VPC conduit issue.
Maya R: Customer impact: Cygnus enterprise tenant experiencing errors for ~40% of requests; latency for successful requests increased 2-3x. They have active traffic in us-west1 only (no multi-region failover on their side). Need to present mitigation options to customer ops.
Jordan K: Mitigations we can do now (ordered):
1) Shift Cygnus traffic to cygnus-dpool-us-east1 warm-capacity (fast path) via traffic-manager route override. 2) DNS failover: update low-TTL record for cygnus.enterprise.redwood -> point to us-east1 LB. 3) Scale up warm pool in us-west1 if CNI stabilizes (slow). 4) Fail open to hosted fallback model (lossy for data residency) - last resort.
Priya S: Is cygnus-dpool-us-east1 primed? I see warm instances but quantization/profile mismatch risk (some models are 4bit-ptq there). We need to ensure model variant compatibility.
Lars E: Quick check: model v2026-03-10 is available in us-east1 (quantized). Behavior differences minimal for this tenant, but we should include a note to customer: slight perf variance possible.
Maya R: Customer comms draft: "We're seeing a regional network disruption impacting your us-west1 dedicated pool. We'll shift traffic to your reserved warm capacity in us-east1 to restore availability. You may see minor differences in latency and output quality for a short period. We'll keep you updated." Approve before I send?
Jordan K: Approve. Also add estimated RTO 10-15m for routing change + DNS propagation. Set TTL to 30s for the DNS cutover to minimize overlap.
SRE Rotation: @Jordan K taking lead on routing change. @Lars E handle kube/CNI remediation in us-west1. @Priya S validate model compatibility & cache priming in us-east1. I'll stay on the loop for handoff in 30m.
Jordan K: Initiating route override now. Command: ``curl -XPOST https://controlplane.redwood/api/traffic-manager/override -d '{"tenant":"cygnus","from":"us-west1","to":"us-east1","sticky":true}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'``
deploy-bot: override request accepted. override_id=ovr-2026-188888-01. Preview: ~85% of traffic will shift within ~60s, remainder from long-lived connections.
Jordan K: Observing traffic shift metrics -> errors drop from 32% -> 6% in 90s. latency back within SLO for most requests. marking mitigation: traffic override to us-east1.
Priya S: Priming KV caches on us-east1: firing synthetic prompt set for Cygnus. code:
```
for f in prompts/*.json; do curl -XPOST https://us-east1.api.redwood/v1/generate -d @${f} -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACTED'; done
```
Priming shows no model mismatch exceptions. outputs look consistent.
Lars E: us-west1 nodes are still flapping but control-plane logs show surge of BGP flaps to internal fabric. CICD shows a recent quagga update deployed ~00:30 UTC. I'm rolling back the BGP agent on gpunode-12..13 to stabilize.
Maya R: Customer update sent: "We have shifted your traffic to warm capacity in us-east1. You should see successful requests now. We're investigating root cause in us-west1 and will notify once resolved." They acknowledged and asked for ETA on full failback.
Jordan K: Recommend not failing back until control-plane BGP flaps are gone and we've observed 30m steady state in us-west1. We'll plan a controlled rollback window.
SRE Rotation: Handoff note for next oncall in 30m:
- Incident: Cygnus us-west1 dedicated pool degraded due to CNI/BGP flaps.
- Current mitigation: traffic override to us-east1 warm pool (override_id=ovr-2026-188888-01).
- Customer impact: errors reduced from ~32% -> ~6%. Minor latency variance.
- Actions in progress: Lars rolling back routing agent; Priya primed caches; Jordan monitoring override metrics.
- Next steps: confirm us-west1 stability for 30m, prepare DNS TTL switch if failback is desired, coordinate scheduled rollback with customer.
Priya S: Also note: we should update routing policy to include cross-region sticky session behavior to avoid split-brain when we switch back.
Lars E: Rollback of quagga done on gpunode-12/13. Nodes returned to Ready state. kube-proxy flaps stopped. Watching metrics.
Jordan K: Metrics show steady state: errors remain low as traffic still in us-east1. us-west1 pod health good. Suggest waiting 45m before incremental traffic shift back to avoid oscillation.
Maya R: I'll draft post-incident note for the customer including timeline, root cause hypothesis (BGP agent regression), mitigation steps, and recommended follow-ups (control-plane rollback validation, increase DNS TTL automation for enterprise customers, runbook update). Will share with oncall before closing.
SRE Rotation: Thanks team. I'll be the incident owner until handoff. if anything spikes, page SRE Rotation.
Maya R: Closing this thread for now — will reopen if we see relapse. :white_check_mark:
